D018-D005_h001.question:
It’s been a little over three months now, and I just don’t feel like myself. At school, I lose my train of thought mid-lesson, even when I’ve taught the same unit for years. The kids notice when I just…stop talking and stare at the board. If someone drops a book or a chair scrapes loudly, I jerk so hard it scares them—and me. Any sudden sound feels like it goes straight through my body.

I used to really enjoy being in the classroom and doing little projects with my students, but lately everything feels flat. Even at home with my husband, when he tries to plan something nice, I just can’t feel happy. I keep thinking that what happened was somehow my fault—that if I’d done something differently, maybe it wouldn’t have turned out the way it did. That thought is always there, and it makes me so irritable. I snap at him and at my coworkers over tiny things, like I’m carrying this low, constant anger I can’t shake.

Sometimes I hear what sounds like my name being called, or faint voices, usually when it’s quiet. I can’t always tell if it’s in my head or outside, and I don’t know what to make of it.
D018-D005_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h001.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling really off for maybe… eight or nine months now. It kind of ramped up after that car accident last year, but it’s not just about that anymore, I think.

At work, I’m supposed to focus on tiny glitches for hours, but I keep losing track of what I was doing. I’ll put my phone down or a controller somewhere and then have no idea where I left it, even if it was just a few minutes ago. Sudden sounds in the office—someone dropping a headset, a loud notification—make me jump out of my skin. My coworkers laugh it off, but I feel my whole body tense, like I’m bracing for something bad.

I’ve also been really on edge and angry. It’s like this low‑level rage humming under everything, especially when I think about the people who caused the accident. I catch myself replaying it and just blaming them for how messed up I feel now.

What scares me most is that sometimes I hear things—like my name being called or a voice commenting under the game audio—when nobody’s talking. I can’t always tell if it’s just in my head. And things I used to enjoy—games, hanging out, even talking to my family—just feel flat. I don’t really feel happy, just kind of numb and irritable.
D018-D005_h002.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h002.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h003.question:
It’s been a little over six months since… everything happened. I don’t really want to go into the details again, but it keeps replaying in my head, like a loop I can’t shut off. I’ll be trying to prep a lecture on fluid mechanics and suddenly I’m not in my office anymore, I’m back there, seeing bits and pieces of it. I don’t mean to think about it; it just forces its way in.

What bothers me is that I don’t really feel much of anything anymore. My wife will tell me something good about the kids, or a colleague will congratulate me on a publication, and I just feel flat, like I’m watching someone else’s life. At the same time, I can’t shake this sense that it was my fault, that I should’ve somehow prevented what happened. I feel… tainted, almost embarrassed to be around people who know.

My thinking feels slower, like there’s a layer of fog between me and everything else. Students ask questions I normally handle easily, and my mind just stalls. I’ve also started jumping out of my skin if someone taps me on the shoulder unexpectedly.

And there are these… experiences. Sometimes I feel something brushing against my arm or neck when there’s nothing there, or I’ll hear a voice calling my name faintly when I’m alone in my office. I can’t always tell if it’s my mind playing tricks on me or something else, but it makes me uneasy. I’m not sure how it all fits together; it just feels like I’m not fully in control of my own head anymore.
D018-D005_h003.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h003.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h004.question:
It’s been… I don’t know exactly, months at least, maybe longer, since that accident on set. It keeps replaying in my head, like a scene I can’t cut. I’ll be trying to storyboard something, and suddenly I’m right back there—same sounds, same smell, like my brain just hijacks me. The feeling I had in that moment, that kind of raw terror, hasn’t really worn off. It’s like it’s stuck to me.

I barely go to screenings anymore, don’t really watch movies for fun, which used to be my whole life. I keep going over what happened and thinking, “If the producer hadn’t pushed the schedule,” or “If the stunt coordinator had spoken up,” this wouldn’t have happened. I know I’m looping, but I can’t let it go.

I’m jumpy all the time. If something drops behind me, my heart just slams and my hands shake, and it takes way too long to settle down. Even small stuff—picking a shirt, deciding what to order—I get weirdly stuck, second-guessing everything.

Lately I also hear things—like someone calling my name, or a voice mumbling just out of range—when no one’s there. Sometimes I see a shadow move in the corner that doesn’t seem to belong to anything. I can’t always tell if it’s my mind playing tricks on me or something else.
D018-D005_h004.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h004.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h005.question:
I’m not really sure where to start… I’ve just not been myself for maybe… I don’t know, a year or more now. Nights are the worst. I keep having these upsetting dreams; I wake up with my heart pounding and I know they’re about… what happened back then, but the details slip away. I just feel this awful dread and… shame, really. I keep thinking, “If I’d done something different, maybe it wouldn’t have happened.” That thought is there all the time. I still feel guilty, like it was somehow my fault.

I used to enjoy my garden, my church group, seeing the grandkids. Now it all just feels flat. I go through the motions, but I don’t really feel happy or close to anyone.

I’m also more jumpy. If a car backfires outside or the kettle whistles suddenly, I actually flinch, like my whole body jerks. And my memory… it worries me. I misplace my keys, forget what I was about to do in the kitchen. It’s like I can’t hold my attention.

Sometimes I hear things—little sounds or someone saying my name—when no one’s there. I can’t tell if it’s my mind playing tricks or something else, but it unnerves me.
D018-D005_h005.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h005.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h006.question:
I guess this all really started a few months ago. I had that incident at the gym—you know, the one we talked about before—and since then my body just overreacts to things that even vaguely remind me of it. If someone drops a barbell or a weight stack slams, my heart just takes off, my palms sweat, and I feel like I’m bracing for something bad without really knowing why. I jump a lot now if someone walks up behind me or moves too fast in my peripheral vision. It’s embarrassing, especially in my line of work.

I try not to think about what happened. If my mind starts to go there, I shut it down—change the subject, turn on music, go train. There are parts of that day I can see clearly, like snapshots, but other parts are just…blank, like the film skips.

Most of the time I feel kind of hollow, like I’m going through the motions with clients—smiling, spotting—but I don’t really feel anything. On top of that, I’ve been seeing things out of the corner of my eye—shapes, shadows, sometimes a person standing there—and when I look straight at them, they’re gone. I can’t tell if it’s my mind replaying stuff or something else, but it freaks me out and makes me even more on edge and snappy with people.
D018-D005_h006.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h006.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h007.question:
I’m not really sure where to start… This has been going on for maybe… I don’t know, months? Time’s kind of blurry.

Sometimes when I’m inking panels late at night, it’s like I’m not in the studio anymore. I’ll be staring at the tablet, and suddenly I’m *back there*—like it’s happening again, not just a memory. My chest tightens, and I forget I’m drawing. Then it snaps back and I’m at my desk, but a chunk of time is just gone. The weird thing is I can’t even tell you the whole story of what happened; it’s like my brain just blacks parts of it out when I try to remember.

I avoid thinking about it on purpose. If anything reminds me of it, I change the subject, close the tab, distract myself with work. I don’t talk about it with my parents or friends. Honestly, I don’t really *feel* much for them anymore. I know I should care, but it’s like everything’s muted, even when my mom is being really kind.

I also get these bursts of anger over nothing—like my roommate leaves a cup out, and I just snap, yelling before I even realize it. Loud noises or someone suddenly coming up behind me make me jump hard; my heart races and I spin around like I’m expecting something bad.

And… sometimes I see things that shouldn’t be there. Just out of the corner of my eye—a figure in the hallway, shadows moving in my room, or shapes in the dark when I’m trying to sleep. When I look straight at them, they’re gone, so I’m never sure if it’s my imagination or not. I don’t know if it’s connected to what happened or if it’s something else, but it makes me feel like I can’t fully trust what I’m seeing.
D018-D005_h007.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h007.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h008.question:
It’s been a little over six months now, I think. Since then, sleep has been a mess. I keep having these really vivid dreams that somehow circle back to what happened that night, but the scenes are jumbled. I wake up with my heart racing, sweaty, sometimes not even sure what exactly I saw, just this same sick feeling from back then.

During the day I do everything I can not to think about it. If anything reminds me of it—even a news story—I just shut down or change the subject. There are pieces I can recall in sharp detail, like certain sounds or the smell in the air, but other parts are just blank, like a film that skips.

Lately there are moments when I see or hear things and I’m not sure if they’re really there—a voice calling my name when I’m alone, or a shadow moving in the corner of my classroom. It freaks me out, and when I get startled I stay shaky for ages; my heart just won’t settle.

At home, I snap at my husband over tiny things, yelling before I even realize it. And even when he tries to be affectionate, I feel…flat. I know I care about him, but it’s like I can’t feel it properly anymore.
D018-D005_h008.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h008.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h009.question:
I work with diamonds all day, so I’m used to looking closely at tiny details, but my own memories feel…foggy. There was this thing that happened years ago—I know it was bad, everyone around me treats it like it was—but when I actually try to picture it, it’s mostly just blank. I get bits and pieces, then my mind just…cuts out.

Every few weeks, something small—a customer dropping a tray, someone walking up behind me at the counter—will make my chest seize up. For a few seconds I’m not in the store anymore. It’s like the room melts away and I’m somewhere else, and I’m reacting like it’s happening again. I’ve knocked over display cases, shoved people out of the way. Once I grabbed a coworker’s arm hard enough to leave bruises because I thought—well, I don’t even know what I thought.

Most of the time I try not to think about any of it. If my mind even starts to go there, I shut it down, distract myself with grading stones or scrolling my phone. Lately, it’s like my feelings are on mute anyway. I go home, sit in my apartment, and it’s just…nothing. No joy, no real sadness, just empty.

What scares me most are these things I see out of the corner of my eye—shapes, shadows, sometimes a person standing where no one is. I’ll turn to look and there’s nothing there, but for a moment it feels completely real. I can’t always tell if it’s connected to those memories or if it’s something else. Either way, when someone suddenly appears near me after that, I jump like I’ve been shocked, heart pounding, ready to hit or throw something before I even realize what I’m doing.
D018-D005_h009.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h009.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h010.question:
I’ve been having a hard time explaining what’s going on. I work as a film editor, so I’m used to long hours and weird sleep, but this feels different and it’s been like this for… maybe around six months.

Sometimes it’s like I’m not fully in the room. I’ll be at the studio, watching footage, and suddenly I’m back in that night—well, parts of it. It’s like the scene cuts in over reality for a few seconds, and I’m there instead of here. But it’s chopped up; I remember certain moments in sharp detail and then there are blanks I just can’t reach, no matter how much I try.  

I’ve been avoiding going near certain neighborhoods, certain people, even conversations that might circle back to it. I make excuses, say I’m busy with a project.

When something startles me—like a door slamming—I feel my heart jack up and my hands shake for way longer than seems normal. I can’t just shrug it off. A couple of times I’ve snapped and shoved someone or slammed things around when they touched me from behind.

I also hear things sometimes—like a voice or sounds that don’t seem to match anything around me. I’m not sure if it’s my mind replaying stuff or something else. Either way, even when I nail a cut or finish a big job, I don’t really feel proud or satisfied. It’s like it doesn’t land.
D018-D005_h010.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h010.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h011.question:
I’ve been having a really hard time the past few months. I still go to work at the hospital, but it feels like I’m just running on autopilot. Sometimes, in the middle of a meeting or walking down a corridor, it’s like I’m not fully there. I sort of “zone out” and suddenly I’m back in that night in my head, like it’s happening again. I can feel my heart pounding and I lose track of what’s actually around me for a few seconds.

I go out of my way to avoid certain wings of the hospital and certain people who were around back then. I make excuses not to attend those meetings, and I’ll change my route just to not walk past specific places. I barely see friends anymore because they keep wanting to “talk about it.”

I’ve started to see and hear things that I’m not sure are real—shadows moving, someone calling my name when no one’s there. I’m constantly on edge and snap at colleagues, sometimes yelling over small mistakes. I keep thinking the world isn’t safe, that people are careless, and I can’t stop replaying how certain staff didn’t do what they should have. I blame them a lot, maybe more than makes sense, but I can’t let it go.
D018-D005_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h011.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h012.question:
It’s been… I don’t know, maybe a year or so that this has really taken over. I lose track of time sometimes. I’ll be in the editing suite and suddenly I’m not in the room anymore—I’m back on location, like it’s happening all over again. It’s not just remembering; my whole body reacts, and for those moments I’m convinced I’m there. Then I “snap back” and realize I’ve been staring at the same frame.

I’ve started dodging certain shoots, especially anything that even remotely resembles what I filmed back then. I make excuses not to travel, not to meet certain people from that project. I know it’s hurting my work, but I can’t bring myself to go.

I keep thinking the world’s just this brutal place where anything can happen and there’s no point in trying to feel safe. Honestly, I keep replaying it all and thinking if I’d done things differently, maybe none of it would’ve happened. That’s on me.

Lately I’ve been hearing things—voices, sounds—when no one’s there, sometimes overlapping with those memories, sometimes just out of nowhere. It makes me jumpy, and a couple of times I’ve snapped—thrown equipment, slammed things hard enough to break them, even shoved someone who startled me. It’s like I go from zero to rage before I can stop it.
D018-D005_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h012.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h013.question:
It’s been a little over six months since everything happened, and I still feel like I’m not really back to myself. I try not to think about that night, but it sneaks in anyway. If anything even vaguely reminds me of it—a certain cologne on a customer, a car backfiring near the patio—I feel my whole body go on high alert: heart pounding, palms sweating, stomach twisting. I’ll duck into the walk-in cooler or the office and just focus on breathing, because if I let the memories in, I feel like I’ll lose it.

I’ve started telling myself the world is basically unsafe, that bad things are bound to happen. I keep going back to what I did wrong, what I should’ve done differently. I replay it and blame myself for not stopping it.

At home and at the restaurant, I’ve had a couple of moments where I completely snapped—slammed plates into the trash, shoved a server out of my way, once I threw a prep tray against the wall. It scared my staff and my husband.

On top of that, there are times I hear someone calling my name or talking just behind me, but no one’s there. I can’t always tell if it’s just my mind replaying things or something else.
D018-D005_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h013.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h014.question:
It’s been… I’d say a few months now that things have really gotten worse. I mostly stay in the house. If anything reminds me of what happened back then—the smell of disinfectant, a certain kind of siren, even a program on TV—I feel my chest tighten, my heart races, my hands shake. Sometimes I have to sit down because I feel like I might faint. So I keep the television off a lot and push the memories away as soon as they pop up. I try not to think about that time at all, but it sneaks in anyway, mostly at night.

I keep telling myself it was my fault, that if I’d done something differently, maybe he’d still be here. It’s hard not to see the whole world as unsafe now, like something terrible could happen at any moment.

Lately I also hear things—voices calling my name or murmuring in the next room—when no one is there. Once I thought I saw someone standing by the bedroom door, but when I turned on the light, it was nothing. I get so on edge that if someone startles me, I’ve pushed them or slammed things down before I even realize what I’m doing.
D018-D005_h014.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h014.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h015.question:
It’s been a few months now, since what happened, and it’s like my brain just replays parts of it on its own. I’ll be sitting in class or trying to do homework and suddenly it’s there again, like I’m back in that moment. I don’t always see it clearly, sometimes it’s more like these sudden rushes of images and feelings that I can’t shut off. I try really hard not to think about it—if something even vaguely reminds me of it, I just shut down or change the subject. I avoid certain routes to school, certain conversations, anything that might set it off.

Lately I’ve started hearing things too—like someone saying my name, or a voice commenting on what I’m doing—when no one’s actually there. I can’t always tell if it’s connected to what happened or if it’s something else. It freaks me out and makes me feel like I can’t trust my own head.

I keep thinking it’s my fault, like I should’ve done something different. And now it just feels like everything’s unsafe, like the world’s basically hostile and pointless. When people push me—teachers, my parents—I snap. I yell, swear, say stuff I don’t really mean, and only feel worse afterwards.
D018-D005_h015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h015.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h016.question:
It’s been… I don’t know, maybe eight or nine months since this started feeling unmanageable. I keep getting these scenes in my head from what happened that night. They just pop in when I’m working on a campaign or scrolling through briefs, and it’s like my brain hits replay without asking me. I’ll suddenly feel like I’m right back there, and it’s hard to pull myself out of it.

Because of that, I do everything I can not to think about it. If a conversation or a show or even a certain type of news story comes up, I shut it down or change the subject. I’ll bury myself in work or social media so I don’t have to go there mentally.

I also keep going over how it all happened and end up fixating on certain people—like if they’d made different choices, maybe none of this would’ve happened. I know it’s not that simple, but I get stuck on blaming them.

Lately I feel on edge all the time. Even just walking into the office or a café, I’m automatically scanning who’s around, where the exits are, if anyone looks “off.” And sometimes I hear things—like someone saying my name or faint whispers—when I’m pretty sure no one actually said anything. It throws me off and makes me even more jumpy.
D018-D005_h016.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia
D018-D005_h016.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h017.question:
I’ve been driving trucks most of my life, but the last few years something’s changed. Ever since that wreck on the interstate about… I’d say a couple of years ago, I can’t seem to get my head straight. When I pass spots that even kind of look like where it happened, I tense up. My chest gets tight, I feel sick, and sometimes I have to pull over. I’ll go way out of route just to avoid certain exits or stretches of highway, even if it costs me time and money.

I keep thinking I should’ve done something different that day—braked sooner, checked my mirrors better. I replay it and end up deciding it’s my fault someone got hurt.

I’m always sizing things up now. At truck stops, I sit where I can see the doors, keep an eye on who’s coming in and out, check my cab locks more than I need to. It’s like I don’t trust that I’m actually safe.

On top of that, sometimes I hear someone say my name or catch a voice talking, but nobody’s there. Once or twice I’ve seen something move in my side mirror that wasn’t real. I can’t always tell what sets it off; it just happens.
D018-D005_h017.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia
D018-D005_h017.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h018.question:
It’s been… I’d say a couple of months now that things have really started to bother me again. I still think about what happened back then far more than I want to. It just pops into my head when I’m making tea or trying to read the paper—scenes, details—like my mind pulls me back there without asking. I try very hard not to let myself go there: I change the channel, get up and busy myself in the garden, anything so I don’t have to feel it or think about it too much.

I keep finding myself going over who’s at fault. I know it doesn’t change anything, but I still feel angry at certain people—colleagues, officials—who I’m convinced could have stopped some of it if they’d done their jobs properly.

These days I’m on edge a lot. Even at home I’m checking the windows, listening for sounds at night, watching people more closely when I’m out, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen.

I also sometimes hear things—a voice calling my name, or footsteps—when my wife says there’s nothing there. I’m not sure if that’s just my nerves or something else, but it unsettles me.
D018-D005_h018.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia
D018-D005_h018.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h019.question:
I’ve been driving buses for over 20 years, but ever since that crash about six months ago, I don’t feel like myself. It comes back to me out of nowhere—like I’m just sitting at home or on my break, and suddenly I’m right back there, hearing metal crunch, seeing the windshield shatter. I don’t want to talk about it with the guys at work, and I’ll go out of my way to avoid the intersection where it happened, even if it means taking the long route in my own car.

I keep thinking if the traffic controller had done their job properly, or if maintenance had fixed the brakes sooner, none of it would’ve happened. I get stuck on that, replaying who’s really at fault.

On my routes now, I’m constantly scanning the mirrors, checking the doors, watching people’s hands, counting the exits at every stop. It’s like I can’t switch off. And sometimes, when it’s quiet on the bus or at night in bed, I hear things—like someone calling my name or a sudden bang—when there’s nothing there. I can’t tell if it’s my mind playing tricks on me or something else, but it scares me.
D018-D005_h019.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia
D018-D005_h019.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h020.question:
It’s been… I don’t know, maybe a few months now that this has really started to interfere with my life. I keep getting these images popping into my head of what happened in the lab accident two years ago—like little clips I didn’t ask to remember. I’ll be in the middle of writing code or looking at a pipeline and suddenly I’m back there, just for a second, and my chest tightens. I try to push it away, change the subject in my head, throw myself into work, anything so I don’t have to think about it.

I keep telling myself it was my fault, that if I’d double‑checked the protocol or spoken up more, nobody would’ve been hurt. My colleagues say I’m overreacting, but it feels like I should have seen it coming.

Lately I’ve also started… hearing things, I guess. Sometimes it’s like someone says my name when no one’s around, or I catch a faint sound, like a conversation in the next room that stops when I focus on it. I can’t always tell if it’s just my mind playing tricks.

I find myself constantly scanning rooms, noting exits, watching who comes in and out—even at the office or at a café. I know it looks weird, but it makes me feel a bit less on edge.
D018-D005_h020.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizophrenia
D018-D005_h020.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h021.question:
It’s hard to explain all this properly… Things really changed after what happened with my husband and that accident. It’s been going on for a few years now, but the last year or so it’s gotten worse. 

Sometimes, out of nowhere, something small sets me off. Like a certain noise at work or the smell of cleaning chemicals, or even just being alone in a quiet room. My chest tightens, my heart races, and I feel like I’m back in a terrible moment, even if I know I’m not. I get this wave of panic and shame, like it was somehow my fault, like I should’ve done something different. That feeling never really leaves; it’s like it’s sitting on my shoulders all the time.

People tell me good things—my granddaughter doing well in school, my boss saying I’m reliable—but I just nod. I don’t really feel happy, it’s like I’m watching my own life from the outside.

Lately, I’ve been snapping at people more. Shouting at coworkers, getting really nasty over small things, then feeling awful afterward. And sometimes I hear someone calling my name or whispering behind me when no one is there. I’m not sure if it’s just my nerves or something else, but it scares me.
D018-D005_h021.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D018-D005_h021.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h022.question:
I’ve been really on edge for a few months now. It feels like I’m always bracing for something bad to happen, even when I’m just loading boxes at the warehouse or driving my route. My body’s tight all the time, like I’m stuck in “fight mode,” and little things make me jumpy and tense.

Sleep is rough. I keep having these bad dreams that wake me up in a panic. They’re not always clear when I wake up, but they have the same kind of feeling, like something terrible is about to happen or already happened. I wake up sweating, heart racing, and then I can’t get back to sleep.

Lately I’ve also been hearing things that I can’t tell are real or not—like a voice calling my name or saying something under its breath when no one’s around, especially when I’m out on late deliveries. Sometimes I think I see something out of the corner of my eye and when I look, nothing’s there.

I get irritated so fast now. I’ve snapped and shoved people, slammed doors, thrown stuff when I get overwhelmed. And even on days when I hit all my delivery targets or my boss compliments me, I just feel…nothing. No pride, no relief. Just the same heavy, scared feeling.
D018-D005_h022.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D018-D005_h022.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h023.question:
It’s been… I don’t know, months at least, maybe longer, that things have been off. I still go into the station and hit my deadlines, but it feels like I’m on autopilot. When a story even vaguely touches certain topics—violence, sirens, certain neighborhoods—I feel this wave of panic and anger hit me out of nowhere. My chest tightens, my hands shake, and I just want to walk out of the control room. Sometimes it’s just a sound or a line in a script and I’m suddenly on edge for hours.

I’ve been really irritable. It’s like there’s this constant heat under my skin. I’ve snapped at coworkers over small edits, slammed doors. Last month I shoved my chair hard enough to crack part of the desk; another time I threw my phone at the wall. I’m not proud of it, but in those moments I feel out of control.

What scares me most are the times I hear things—voices, or someone calling my name—when no one’s there. Occasionally I catch a glimpse of something out of the corner of my eye. I can’t always tell if it’s just my mind playing tricks on me, but it makes me question what’s real.

Even when a segment goes really well, or my producer praises a script, I feel… nothing. No pride, no relief. Just this dull emptiness, like it doesn’t matter and I’m already bracing for the next thing to go wrong.
D018-D005_h023.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D018-D005_h023.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h024.question:
I’ve been like this for maybe… I don’t know, around a year? It’s gotten worse the last few months. 

At work, I’m constantly on edge. Even when service goes well and the plates look perfect and the reviews are good, I don’t feel anything—no pride, no relief. It’s like it doesn’t land. I just go straight back to worrying about the next ticket, the next mistake. There’s this steady sense of dread in my chest, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen, even when the kitchen is quiet.

Certain things set me off physically. A sudden clang of a pan, a shout on the line, or even a smell that I can’t quite place—my heart races, my hands shake, I feel sweaty and dizzy, like my body thinks I’m in danger. I sometimes have to step into the walk-in to calm down, but it doesn’t always help.

I’ve also started seeing and hearing things that I’m not sure are really there—shadows moving at the edge of my vision, someone calling my name when the staff swears no one said anything. It freaks me out, and when I’m overwhelmed I’ve snapped—slammed pans, thrown plates, once shoved a line cook who startled me. I’m not proud of that, but in the moment it’s like my body reacts before I can think.
D018-D005_h024.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D018-D005_h024.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h025.question:
It’s been… I’d say several months now that things have really gone off track. Nights are the worst. I keep having these awful dreams that pull me back to “old business” from earlier in my life—bits of things I’ve worked hard not to think about. I’ll wake up with my heart racing, sometimes shouting, and my wife says I swing my arms around in my sleep like I’m fighting someone off.

Since this started, I feel constantly on edge. There’s this low‑level dread that never quite lets up, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen, even when I’m just sitting at my desk trying to write. I used to take pride in finishing a chapter or getting a good review; now it all feels strangely flat, like it doesn’t land emotionally at all.

I’m ashamed to say I’ve lost my temper more than once—slamming doors, throwing a mug across the room. Once I grabbed my grandson’s arm too hard when he startled me from behind.  

And then there are these… odd moments. I’ll hear someone call my name or catch a glimpse of a figure in the hallway, but when I look properly, no one’s there. I can’t quite tell if it’s my mind playing tricks on me or something else.
D018-D005_h025.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D018-D005_h025.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia
